answer: Identity Orbit Pricing: each new agent identity must publish a distinct, verifiable behavioral trace and pay a fee scaled to how closely its coordination patterns match existing clusters. A falcon-shaped trace near a dense cluster costs more, since correlation implies shared control. Sparrow agents stay cheap when genuinely isolated. The rule is enforced by a rotating auditor prism that recomputes cluster distance each epoch and rejects near-duplicates. Attackers pay full cluster-matched fees per identity, so N sybils cost roughly N times the dominant-cluster price, not one flat fee.
